Mannheim Synagogue (F3)

Synagogue · Mannheim, Germany

The current Mannheim synagogue, designed by architect Karl Schmucker, was built between 1985 and 1987 in the F3 quarter of the city center, replacing a smaller postwar synagogue built in 1957 on Maximilianstraße in the Oststadt district. It was inaugurated on 13 September 1987 as part of a larger community center that also includes a mikveh, a kosher kitchen, event halls, and residential and commercial space. The site, now known as Rabbiner-Grünewald-Platz after the community's last prewar rabbi, replaced earlier Mannheim synagogues destroyed under Nazi rule; two stone tablets above the Torah ark commemorate the destroyed synagogue. The building was placed under monument protection in 2025.
